title: The Rock of Ares

panels.visual: The bare, polished grey rock of the Areopagus just below the Acropolis, the Parthenon above it, Glauka the owl perched on the rock
panels.caption: This slippery rock below the Acropolis is the Areopagus: the Rock of Ares, god of war.

panels.visual: Ares (god of war, crested bronze helmet, red cloak) charging with his spear at a young man who is grabbing at a frightened girl by a spring
panels.caption: The myth says a son of the sea god Poseidon attacked Ares' daughter. Ares killed him.

panels.visual: Poseidon (sea-green beard, trident) furious, pointing at Ares; the other gods arriving and sitting on the rock in a circle like judges
panels.caption: Poseidon demanded justice. So the gods sat on this rock and held a trial.

panels.visual: The gods raising their hands to vote; Ares walking away free, relieved
panels.caption: Ares was let off. It was called the first murder trial ever, and the rock was named after him.

panels.visual: A young prince, Orestes, standing in a dark palace hall with a sword, the shadow of his mother Queen Clytemnestra falling across the floor, red drips
panels.caption: Much later a prince, Orestes, came home. His mother Clytemnestra had murdered his father, so Orestes killed her.

panels.visual: Three Furies, snake-haired spirits of revenge with bat wings and long black robes, chasing the terrified Orestes over mountains and seas
panels.caption: Then the Furies, spirits of revenge, hunted him day and night.

panels.visual: Orestes on trial on this rock before a jury of ordinary Athenian men, the goddess Athena presiding in her helmet, the Furies accusing
panels.caption: He fled to Athens. Athena put him on trial here, before a jury of Athenians.

panels.visual: Jurors dropping black and white pebbles into two urns; the pebbles counted out in two exactly equal piles
panels.caption: They voted with pebbles: black for guilty, white for free. Exactly even.

panels.visual: Athena dropping one shining white pebble onto the pile; Orestes looking up in disbelief
panels.caption: Athena cast the deciding vote: white. Orestes walked free.

panels.visual: Athena leading the calmed Furies into a cave under the rock, the Furies' faces softening
panels.caption: Athena gave the Furies a home in a cave under this rock, and they calmed down.

panels.visual: AD 51: Saint Paul (short, balding, dark pointed beard, red-brown travelling cloak) standing on the rock speaking to a crowd of curious Athenian philosophers in cloaks
panels.caption: History now: in AD 51 a traveller, Saint Paul, stood here and told the Athenians about his new faith.

speech.speaker: Paul
speech.text: Men of Athens, I see you are very religious.

panels.visual: Today: a bronze plaque with Greek writing at the foot of the rock, worn ancient steps cut into the stone beside modern metal stairs, two girls and Glauka the owl
panels.caption: His speech is on the bronze plaque at the foot of the steps. Careful: the rock is polished slippery by millions of feet.

mood: Dramatic mood: stormy skies, torchlight, the Furies frightening (snake hair, bat wings, long black robes), one dark-red accent colour; suitable for children aged 9 to 11.
